about:
Rice Equipment Service, Inc. was founded in 1990 in Springfield, Missouri. The company began as a specialist in commercial kitchen equipment repair, establishing itself in the local food service market. No founder names or ownership structure are disclosed in public records.

The company provides repair and maintenance services for a wide range of commercial kitchen equipment. Its offerings include 24-hour emergency service, warranty repair work on virtually all restaurant equipment, and scheduled maintenance calls. Technicians perform on-site diagnostics and repairs for cooking, refrigeration, and food preparation machinery, supporting both new and aging equipment fleets.

Rice Equipment Service works with equipment manufacturers, independent restaurants, and large commercial food operations such as institutional cafeterias and catering facilities. The customer base spans the commercial food service sector across the Springfield region and surrounding areas.

The firm emphasizes prompt, reliable response times and deep familiarity with multiple equipment brands as its core differentiators, positioning itself as a go-to resource for minimizing downtime in professional kitchens. Its 24-hour emergency capability is highlighted as a key service for time-sensitive kitchen failures.

name: Richards Manufacturing
old_description: Richards has proudly served the energy distribution industry since 1945, earning the respect of customers and competitors alike. To have remained successful after all these years, in a demanding and competitive industry, is no simple task. It takes a lot of hard work, starting with our CEO, who oversees operations everyday…and finishing with the individuals on the production lines, who carefully craft every Richards product. They all share one common focus: satisfying the needs of you, our customer. You want reliability — we manufacture top-quality products that exceed your expectations. You want flexibility — Richards designs, manufactures, and tests many non-standard and specialty products to meet our customers’ requirements. Most of all, you want a trusted partner and you can always rely on Richards to assist you with any problem or emergency in the field.
about:
Richards Manufacturing has operated from Irvington, New Jersey, since its founding in 1945. The company began as a family‑owned business producing a single style of underground connector and has remained under family ownership through its evolution into a multi‑line supplier.

Today the firm designs, manufactures, and tests a broad range of electrical and gas distribution equipment. Its product lines include compression lugs and splices, split‑tinned connectors, medium‑voltage loadbreak and deadbreak elbows (5–35 kV), cold‑shrink terminations, network protectors (800–5,100 A), and natural‑gas meter connections, manifold assemblies, and prefabricated meter installations. Production relies on advanced injection‑molding processes and a high‑voltage test laboratory at the Irvington facility. The company also reconditions utility‑owned network protectors and supplies replacement components. Through its ETI division, Richards provides microprocessor‑based network protector relays (MNPR®), monitoring sensors, and SCADA communications enclosures, with more than 20 major utilities worldwide using the MNPR® system.

Richards serves electric and gas utilities, commercial and industrial customers, and natural‑gas distribution companies. Its network protectors and monitoring systems are deployed by major utilities across the globe, while its connector and medium‑voltage products are specified for underground and overhead distribution networks.

The company emphasizes flexibility in meeting non‑standard and specialty requirements, positioning itself as a partner for field emergencies and custom solutions. Its claim as the largest producer of network protectors and accessories underscores its scale in that niche.

about:
Richardson Furniture Mfr is a family-owned furniture manufacturer based in Phoenix, Arizona. The company was founded in 1972 by George and Louise Richardson, who purchased a small local furniture manufacturing plant after working there themselves. The business has remained in the family for three generations, with their youngest son Dean and his wife Stacie taking over in the early 2000s, and their children Shelbee and Christian now also involved.

The company produces upholstered living room furniture, including sofas, sectionals, accent chairs, and custom made-to-order pieces. Its manufacturing processes feature benchcraft upholstery, corner-blocked solid wood frames, and center-match cutting for made-to-order items. The shop employs a team whose members average more than 15 years of experience, though total headcount and facility size are not disclosed.

Richardson Furniture serves the residential furniture market, selling directly to families and through retail channels. Its collections — Richardson Collection, Hunter Leanne Home Collection, and Leather Applications — span styles from Southwest to mid-century modern.

The Richardsons emphasize quality craftsmanship as their defining trait, citing benchcraft construction, solid wood framing, and precise pattern matching as differentiators. The company was started to bring durable, stylish comfort to homes, a mission that continues under the current generation.

name: Richelieu Foods Inc
old_description: For more than a century, Richelieu Foods has built its legacy on craftsmanship, commitment, and partnership. Founded in 1862, we’ve grown from a regional operation into a trusted private brand manufacturer known across retail, co-manufacturing, co-packing and foodservice channels.
about:
Richelieu Foods was founded in 1862 in Beaver Dam, Wisconsin, beginning as a regional operation before evolving into a private-brand manufacturer. In 2018, the company joined the Freiberger Group, a wholly owned subsidiary of Südzucker AG, expanding its reach to a network of 11 locations across Europe and the United States.

The company specializes in private-label pizza programs for retail, co-manufacturing, co-packing, and foodservice channels. Its in-house R&D team applies market research and trend analysis to develop products, while flexible manufacturing and packaging options support efficient production at scale.

Richelieu Foods serves national retailers, foodservice operators, and brands seeking private-label frozen pizza and deli solutions. Customers include retailers and manufacturers that rely on the company to scale private brand offerings, reduce risk, and accelerate growth.

The company emphasizes a partnership-driven model, offering tailored co-creation, pricing analysis, consumer insights, and trend monitoring. It treats each client's label as its own, aiming to deliver seamless customization and reliable execution from concept to full-scale production.

name: Ripple's Auto Parts
old_description: Ripple's Service provides used car and light truck parts for both foreign and domestic vehicles. Our office is located in the heart of Upper Marlboro, Maryland where we have operated since 1947. We have always been, and continue to be, a family owned and operated business with deep roots in the area.
about:
Ripple's Auto Parts operates from Upper Marlboro, Maryland, where it has been located since 1947. The business is family-owned and operated, with deep roots in the local community.

The company supplies used car and light truck parts for both foreign and domestic vehicles. It recycles vehicle parts and functions as a wholesaler for late-model auto and light truck components. Customers can search an online parts inventory by year, make, and model, and the sales staff assists with identifying interchangeable parts across makes and models.

Ripple's serves automotive repair shops, wholesale buyers, and individual vehicle owners seeking replacement parts. Its inventory ranges from small, hard-to-find components to full front-end assemblies, and the company emphasizes its ability to locate parts that may not be immediately in stock.

The business distinguishes itself through its long-standing family ownership, its recycling operation that reclaims usable components, and its willingness to help customers determine part compatibility across different vehicle platforms.

name: Riverland Industries, Inc.
old_description: Since opening in 1999 as a manufacturer of dry ATH, our story has been one of constant expansion and evolution. We’ve been growing for over 25 years — and every year marks an exciting new development in our capabilities. Here are just some of the highlights.
about:
Riverland Industries, Inc. opened in 1999 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, as a manufacturer of dry aluminum trihydrate (ATH). The company has expanded steadily over more than 25 years, evolving from a single-product operation into a full-service toll manufacturer. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

Today Riverland operates as an industrial toll manufacturer, offering custom material processing across a range of unit operations. Its capabilities include size reduction, size separation, heat treating, impregnation, forming, blending, extrusion, particle size reduction, flash calcination, and granulation. Key equipment includes an indirect rotary kiln capable of product temperatures up to 815 °C and air classifiers for fine particle separation. An in-house laboratory provides moisture analysis, particle size distribution, surface area measurement, and porosimetry. The facility also provides warehousing, packaging, and freight management, with direct access to river, rail, and interstate transportation corridors. Headcount is listed as two employees in public records.

The company serves customers in petrochemical, chemical, food-grade, air purification, and water treatment markets. It specializes in adsorbent materials and has produced spherical alumina for a global producer. Partners typically engage Riverland for collaborative process engineering, flexible capital investment, and the design and deployment of dedicated equipment and facilities.

Riverland emphasizes scalable infrastructure and a flexible capital investment model that allows partner-driven expansion. Its collaborative process engineering approach and direct multimodal logistics access are cited as key differentiators, enabling fast, cost-efficient transport and customized facility design.

name: Rivers Metal Products
old_description: Rivers Metal Products, an established metal fabricator and distributor of high-quality metal products, is founded on the principles of hard work, integrity, and commitment to customer service. We intend to serve by developing strong and lasting relationships, utilizing our creative talent, and the latest technologies. We will continue to grow and prosper by improving the quality of life for our customers, employees, suppliers, and community, all of who are valued partners. Their well being is the measure of our success.
about:
Rivers Metal Products was founded in 1973 in Lincoln, Nebraska. The company began as a metal fabrication shop and has since expanded into rotational mold manufacturing and metal distribution.

The company provides custom metal fabrication, rotational mold tooling and repair, contract manufacturing, architectural and interior metalwork, signage, and fine art fabrication. Its shop is equipped for MIG, TIG, arc, and resistance welding; laser, plasma, and flame cutting; shearing, sawing, plate rolling, tube bending, pipe coiling, brake pressing, lathe and mill machining. Rivers Metal also stocks and distributes steel, stainless steel, aluminum, galvanized, polished, brushed, and hot- and cold-rolled sheet metal.

Rivers Metal serves industrial, architectural, artistic, and agricultural clients. Longtime partner Peregrine, Inc. has collaborated for more than 30 years. The firm has fabricated 22,000-gallon rotational molds, agricultural tanks, machinery components, stairways, railings, and public art installations such as the “Backyard Oasis” project for Loeck Designs and community pride sculptures.

The company says its differentiator lies in its consultative approach—guiding customers from material selection through design and production—and its half-century of experience pioneering fabricated stainless-steel rotational molds. Its mission emphasizes hard work, integrity, and customer service, aiming to improve quality of life for customers, employees, suppliers, and the community.

about:
Roadrunner Fabrication, Inc. was founded in 1985 in Denver, Colorado. The company has been Colorado-owned and operated since its inception, serving the western United States with metal fabrication and processing services.

The shop provides a full range of metal fabrication services, including cutting, forming, welding, and assembly, along with powder coating, design assistance, material procurement, and installation. All operations—from design through final coating—are performed on the plant floor, allowing the company to handle projects from prototype to finished installation without outsourcing.

Roadrunner works with customers of all sizes, from national franchise accounts to local construction projects and domestic undertakings. The company emphasizes that it imposes no minimum charge, making its services accessible for small jobs as well as large-scale production runs.

The firm distinguishes itself through speed, responsiveness, and flexibility, claiming that its integrated in-house capabilities enable faster turnaround than other Colorado fabricators. This focus on rapid, end-to-end delivery was a founding principle and remains central to its operation.

about:
Rock Creek Molding, Inc. operates from Glenwood, Arkansas. The company traces its roots to 1986 when its founder began building plastic injection molds; the business was formally established in 1991 and added injection molding capabilities in 1997. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The shop provides plastic injection molding services spanning rapid injection molding and production tooling, along with in‑house mold building. Secondary operations include CNC milling, drilling, tapping, and turning, plus assembly, packaging, and warehousing for select parts. The facility handles runs as small as several hundred pieces up to multi‑million‑part programs; one customer reference notes more than five million parts shipped over a 13‑year period. Headcount and plant size are not published.

Rock Creek serves manufacturers needing custom and standard plastic components across a range of industries, though specific sectors are not listed on its site. The company emphasizes flexibility for both short‑run prototype work and long‑term production contracts.

The firm highlights its quality commitment through 100 % inspection of every part and the ability to waive tooling charges on certain quotes. Its rapid‑tooling approach targets customers who need functional prototypes or low‑volume production without the lead time and expense of traditional hardened tooling.
